tracks.note: A love song from TEAM BABY.
tracks.description: “EVERYTHING” is a love song from TEAM BABY. It first came out as a single in 2016, a year before the album.
tracks.sourceName: The Black Skirts — TEAM BABY on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: A whole world in a room
paragraphs: For a song called EVERYTHING, the scene is intimate: two people in a room on a rainy day, with little need to speak. The scale of the declaration comes from how completely that ordinary company fills the speaker’s attention.

Affection includes the other person’s less polished moments. There is a fondness for being close enough to see them without ceremony, which gives the repeated declaration its warmth. The lyric makes devotion feel domestic and familiar; very little has to happen for the time together to matter.

tracks.performance: SERENADE concert · Sogang University Mary Hall · 2019
tracks.note: Run with Me, live at SERENADE.
tracks.description: Here’s “Run with Me” at sunwoojunga’s SERENADE concert, shared on her own channel. The song comes from her 2019 album Serenade; this performance was recorded at Sogang University’s Mary Hall.

lyricNotes.heading: Someone who will go with you
paragraphs: The invitation to escape comes with room for exhaustion. The person being addressed can cry, move slowly and take the time they need. The speaker offers to accompany them without requiring an explanation of everything that has gone wrong.

There is also a return in the lyric’s imagined journey. Leaving can be temporary, a pause made possible by someone willing to stay beside you. That gives the reassurance a patient quality: the companion remains present through the difficult part, before anything is fixed.

tracks.performance: Begin Again Open Mic · Official live performance
tracks.note: A quiet moment with Car, the garden.
tracks.description: Here’s Car, the garden singing “Tree” for Begin Again’s Open Mic series. The song first came out as a single in April 2019.
tracks.sourceName: Car, the garden — Tree on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: Finding room for awkwardness
paragraphs: The beloved becomes a dancing tree, and the speaker becomes the rough music within it. The pairing gives awkwardness somewhere to belong. The speaker imagines even their timid fears becoming part of an affectionate picture when they are beside this person.

Asking for a smile suggests how much that acceptance matters. The lyric treats closeness as permission to bring an uncertain, unpolished self into a relationship. Its tenderness comes from the hope that someone can receive those parts with affection.

tracks.note: A song about finding a place among others.
tracks.description: “Forest” is about feeling small among other people, and finding a place with them. Choi Yu Ree wrote it for her 2022 single release Stroll. This version is from a Bugs-ker live session.
tracks.sourceName: Choi Yu Ree — Stroll on Apple Music

extraSources.label: Bugs — Stroll release notes and credits

lyricNotes.heading: Wanting to be a place for someone
paragraphs: The wish to become a forest carries a question about belonging. The speaker wants to offer someone a place to enter and stay, while remaining uneasy about their own place among the trees. A generous wish and a sense of inadequacy occupy the same image.

The lyric keeps returning to uncertainty, including whether this place is a forest or a sea. That shifting landscape leaves the speaker’s own position unsettled. Offering shelter does not mean they feel secure themselves; the longing to be recognised remains part of the care they want to give.

tracks.note: Eternal love, from the Bloom concert.
tracks.description: Ahn Ji-young sings “Eternal love” (사랑할 수밖에) at BOL4’s 2024 Bloom concert in this clip from her own channel. The song is from the 2023 EP Merry Go Round.
tracks.sourceName: BOL4 — Merry Go Round - EP on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: When love asks for restraint
paragraphs: The speaker can only clasp their own hands while watching someone they love from a distance. The gesture holds back a desire to give everything, alongside a fear that their own wants might hurt the person they hope to protect.

The devotion in Eternal love includes taking a step back. Its repeated certainty of loving someone sits beside uncertainty about what that love should ask of them. Restraint makes the affection ache: the desire to draw closer persists through the effort to keep it from becoming a burden.

tracks.note: An early song, in front of a live audience.
tracks.description: “RomanceYouthLove” was one of ESEGYE’s first releases. This recording is from their first BLIND concert at Veloso Hongdae, shared by the band themselves.
tracks.sourceName: ESEGYE — Cry For Me / RomanceYouthLove - Single on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: Setting off without a destination
paragraphs: Romance, youth and love become boats in this song’s central image: things that can carry two people somewhere together. Their destination stays unknown. The repeated reassurance draws its confidence from companionship, even as the lyric admits how little they know.

That admission keeps the optimism a little reckless. Youth appears as a willingness to depart before having an answer, with another person close enough to share the uncertainty. The promise depends on their togetherness; the world ahead has offered no guarantees.

tracks.description: “The Wave” keeps going after the last vocal line, with an extended instrumental ending. This version comes from the 2020/NEON concert, filmed at YES24 Live Hall on December 7, 2019.
tracks.sourceName: SE SO NEON — Summer Plumage - EP on Apple Music
tracks.listeningNote: The song first came out as a single in September 2017, then appeared on Summer Plumage the following month.

lyricNotes.heading: A departure with no explanation
paragraphs: The Wave gives its brief parting scene a dreamlike strangeness: the departing figure is associated with the moon. There is no explanation of who this person is or what has happened between them and the speaker.

That missing context leaves space around the farewell. The lyric holds an image in view without turning it into a complete relationship story, so its emotional distance remains hard to settle. A reading of loss is possible, but the words keep the circumstances open.

tracks.note: Letting go, and hoping to be remembered.
tracks.description: “ONCE” is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. Yu Dabin describes that farewell in the band’s release interview for the October 2023 single.
tracks.listeningNote: Yu Dabin made the cover herself, drawing over a photograph of her own hand. She left the thing held inside unnamed, so it could mean something different to each listener.

extraSources.label: YdBB — ONCE interview and artwork story

lyricNotes.heading: Hoping to be remembered kindly
paragraphs: ONCE looks back at the moment affection began while speaking from the edge of a goodbye. The speaker wants a place in the other person’s memory, even as distance grows between them.

That wish gives the farewell its tenderness and its uncertainty: nobody can choose how they will be remembered. Regret remains, alongside a hope that distance need not erase their bond. The song makes room for an attachment that continues as two people grow apart, without promising that affection will bring them back together.

tracks.note: One of the band’s early songs.
tracks.description: “Don’t feel sad” comes from WhiteUsedSocks’ early days. Jung Jaeheon wrote and composed the song, released in June 2017, before The Little Match Boy and Through Yearning.
tracks.sourceName: WhiteUsedSocks — Don’t feel sad on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: A wish made through regret
paragraphs: Memories arrive before the speaker has chosen to revisit them. The lyric’s wish for the other person to feel less sad is complicated by an admission of having been absorbed in their own feelings. Looking back brings affection and responsibility together.

That regret changes the force of the title. The reassurance can be heard as a hope for someone’s happiness from someone conscious of their own past selfishness. The wish is modest: to let a memory bring a smile again, even with regret still attached to it.

tracks.description: “Don’t run away” was part of the September 2018 soundtrack to A-TEEN. It’s an easy place to meet Motte’s music, even if you’ve never seen the series.
tracks.sourceName: Motte — A-TEEN Part.4 on Apple Music

lyricNotes.heading: Trust after words go wrong
paragraphs: Two people keep trying to get closer and somehow end up further apart. The speaker recognises that their clumsy words have hurt the other person, then asks for the trust that might let them speak more openly.

There is worry beneath the repeated assurance of mutual belief: the speaker fears being left alone and keeps looking for an answer. Asking about the other person’s day brings the plea down to an ordinary conversation. Repair might begin with hearing what has been difficult, rather than finding a perfect declaration.

tracks.note: On letting go and getting through the day.
tracks.description: “Even if you leave” is about the things that are hard to let go of, and the habit of blaming yourself after they’re gone. HANRORO wrote both the words and music.
tracks.sourceName: HANRORO — Even if you leave on Apple Music
tracks.listeningNote: Her release note leaves room for more than a breakup: it could be a choice, a neglected relationship or something you keep turning over in your mind. The song came out in April 2023.

extraSources.label: HANRORO — release notes and credits on POCLANOS

lyricNotes.heading: The pull of self-blame
paragraphs: The Korean title, 자처, carries the sense of bringing something upon oneself. Alongside the English title Even if you leave, it places separation next to responsibility. The speaker’s difficulty letting go becomes tangled with the thought that their pain is their own doing.

In her release note, HANRORO leaves the addressee open: it could be a person, a past choice or something that traps the self. She describes writing the song to stop feeding self-blame. That context makes the lyric’s guilt a feeling under examination, rather than a verdict that the speaker deserves to suffer.

tracks.note: A love song with mixed feelings.
tracks.description: “Someone” holds affection and doubt together. It’s from Kim Sawol’s second album, Romance, released in September 2018.
tracks.sourceName: Kim Sawol — Romance on Apple Music
tracks.listeningNote: In the album notes, love is a way of getting to know yourself, even when you know it may end. That mix of closeness and loneliness runs through Romance.

lyricNotes.heading: Reassurance with doubt underneath
paragraphs: Much of Someone addresses another person as precious and loved. Then the lyric turns towards the speaker’s own lonely night. The confidence of the reassurance becomes more complicated once the person offering it admits feeling unloved.

That change of perspective leaves tenderness and doubt close together. Being able to recognise someone else’s worth does not make it easy to feel your own. The speaker can offer conviction to another person while still needing to hear something like it themselves.

tracks.note: 0310, from Every letter I sent you.
tracks.description: “0310” is sung in English, with the words on screen in Baek’s own lyric video. It’s from her 2019 album Every letter I sent you.
tracks.sourceName: Yerin Baek — Every letter I sent you. on Apple Music
tracks.listeningNote: Baek describes the album as a collection of thoughts and memories from ages nineteen to twenty-three. “0310” has acoustic guitar, strings and a full band behind her voice. “Square (2017)” is on the same album if you’d like another song.
tracks.credits: Written and composed by Yerin Baek. Arranged by Yerin Baek & Cloud.

extraSources.label: Korean Music Awards — Album of the Year, 2020
Yerin Baek — official 0310 lyric video and credits

lyricNotes.heading: Trying to sound less attached
paragraphs: 0310 is sung in English, and its hesitations are part of the story. The speaker tries to sound casual about someone leaving, then admits how much that possibility frightens them. What appears indifferent at first becomes a way of protecting a much stronger attachment.

The lyric circles around things left unsaid and the wish to seem fine. Its vulnerability comes through the gap between the position the speaker wants to hold and the reassurance they keep asking for. The contradictions allow embarrassment, defensiveness and affection to remain audible in the words.

tracks.note: A bloom that doesn’t look like a flower.
tracks.description: The speaker in “Flower” hoped to bloom, but compares themselves to mold in a damp room. The song pairs that harsh self-image with a wish to keep growing and be loved. This is the official recording from gongwon’s EP 0.
tracks.credits: Lyrics by gongwon; music by gongwon and Bae Do Hyub; arranged by Bae Do Hyub. First released as a single on 30 January 2026, then included on 0 on 24 February 2026.

extraSources.label: gongwon — 0 full live session and chapter list

lyricNotes.heading: Growing in a damp room
paragraphs: The official English title is Flower, while 곰팡이 means “mold.” The difference matters to a speaker who expected one kind of growth and sees another in themselves. A damp room gives that disappointment a physical setting: what grows there is shaped by its conditions.

The harsh self-description is part of the speaker’s struggle with worth. Continuing to grow has not brought an easy sense of pride, yet the wish to be loved persists. The lyric holds that wish beside the feelings the speaker finds difficult to accept, leaving self-acceptance unfinished.

tracks.koreanTitle: 불안한 내 맘 달랠 곳은 너밖에 없어
tracks.performance: Rolling 31st anniversary concert · Official live clip
tracks.description: In “Only You”, a walk through Seoul Forest brings a changed relationship into focus. The speaker still wants comfort from the person they struggle to face. Yebit sings it here at the Rolling 31st anniversary concert.
tracks.sourceName: Yebit — Only You on Apple Music
tracks.credits: Lyrics, music and arrangement by Choi Hong-gyu (Rebuild). The single was released on 20 February 2024; this live clip was uploaded on 12 February 2026.

extraSources.label: Genie — Only You: lyrics and credits
MAGIC STRAWBERRY SOUND — official live clip and performance details

lyricNotes.heading: When the place stays the same
paragraphs: Seoul Forest remains familiar while the relationship has changed. Walking there alone makes the difference harder to ignore: a shared place can keep reminding someone of a closeness that no longer feels secure.

The speaker tries to look all right, with a smile that conceals hurt. The person they find painful to face is also the person they want to lean on. That makes the request for comfort unresolved; affection and distress lead back to the same person, and outward composure gives little indication of what remains inside.

tracks.description: In “Breath”, guitar leaves plenty of space around Yoon Mirae’s voice. The song is about the ordinary things that remind you of someone after a breakup.
tracks.note: An acoustic R&B song with room to breathe.
tracks.credits: Composed by Yoon Mirae & Tiger JK. Lyrics by Tiger JK.
tracks.sourceName: Yoon Mirae — Breath on Apple Music

extraSources.label: Korean Music Awards — Best R&B & Soul Album, 2008
Korean Music Awards — Best R&B & Soul Song, 2008

lyricNotes.heading: Warmth that outlasts a goodbye
paragraphs: A scarf carries the absent person into an ordinary winter day. Its colour has faded, but the warmth remains useful. The object makes memory tangible: something given in the past can still offer comfort after the relationship has changed.

The speaker’s small, private smile can coexist with pain. Winter keeps bringing the other person to mind, without settling what happens next. The tenderness lies in that continued presence in daily life, where missing someone and feeling grateful for their warmth have become difficult to separate.

listeningGuides.intro: Some songs, live performances and a little about the people behind them. A place to start if Korean music is new to you.
paragraphs: There’s a love song by The Black Skirts, a farewell from YdBB and a live version of SE SO NEON’s The Wave that carries on long after the singing ends. You can dip in wherever you like.

You don’t need to know Korean to spend time here. Yerin Baek’s 0310 is sung in English, and each song’s artist page has English notes on the meaning and mood of its lyrics. More artists appear below, with new additions as the journal grows.

trackNotes.black-skirts: The Black Skirts is Bryan Cho’s solo project. EVERYTHING is a love song that first came out in 2016, before joining the album TEAM BABY a year later. The official music video is here, and the album is linked on his artist page if you’d like more.
trackNotes.yerin-baek: 0310 is sung in English, with lyrics on screen in Yerin Baek’s own video. It comes from Every letter I sent you., an album she describes as a collection of thoughts and memories from ages nineteen to twenty-three. Square (2017) is another song from the same record.
trackNotes.ydbb: YdBB are a five-piece band built around singer-songwriter Yu Dabin, playing music that moves between acoustic folk and rock. ONCE is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. It’s a farewell she talks about in the band’s release interview.
trackNotes.hanroro: In Even if you leave, HANRORO writes about the things that are hard to let go of. Her release note describes being caught between blaming someone else and blaming yourself, and trying to get through the day without making that feeling worse.
trackNotes.se-so-neon: Hwang Soyoon’s voice and guitar are at the centre of SE SO NEON’s The Wave. This version was filmed at the 2020/NEON concert in December 2019. After the last vocal line, the performance carries on with a long instrumental ending.
